summary: The long view keeps its own beat: lamps down the verges, and the chorale lit a minute off
BWV 645's beat now lands where the music does: the edition's pickup was hiding in the MIDI file
The Passacaglia's wheel takes its own pulse: a tooth per beat on the rim
Every piece gets its own bell: struck size and length measured from the music
Play along: click on the pulse of the piece, and the room rings
BWV 582 is a wheel: it turns once to the ground bass, and the rim counts the turns
BWV 565 is a fugue now: the subject is gold, and you can see it coming
BWV 645's chorale now blooms at its three real arrivals, not at every breath
BWV 645 is a long road now: the whole piece on one screen, and the chorale can be seen coming
BWV 639 is woven, not falling: a phrase to a screen, and the repeat glows gold
Every note speaks through a rank of pipes now, and the loudest moment is measured
Pause, restart and moving anywhere into the piece — and the notes are really drawn
All four pieces play, each line once and at the right octave
BWV 565 plays in full, the notes fall as light
